_note: 献精室 (the content of #113-#115; the owner's decisions there, version 2: #115's P+ of 2026-11-09): the scoring's own numbers - the app's source of truth (Kensei / KenseiCore), read as well by tools/kensei_sim.py and bridge/tests/test_kensei_data.py, so the three count alike. version: written into every run's record with the whole of this file (a run is scored by the rules it began with: a run of version 1 - unit combo - goes on and is read back as version 1). unit: what a weak spot is - play (a play itself; version 1: combo). A move's grade by the weak items, each judged on its own, the highest kept: big - the weak play itself, combo - another play of the same combo (part and lead both), near - one of the two, non - none. Its rise by the grade, the gauge to threshold makes him come: its amount = base of the grade x (1 +/- tolerance, drawn from the run's seed; 0 by default - the owner's decision) + what went past the threshold (the overkill, 1 to 1, taken before the gauge goes back to 0). decay: a non move's rise x factor for each time its combo was used so under the same assignment (cumulative, no recovery, cleared at a redraw), rounded, at least floor. The turn limit: the fewest turns to the need knowing the answer (every grade, the worst tolerance; at least what big moves alone take) + the search allowance: the candidates' axis values (their parts + their leads) / the weak count x per_axis_value + the plays of the largest combo x per_play (tried one by one: not split by the weak count), a redraw (vary) adding per_redraw of both again, x the tightening - at least 1 (the simulation of 2026-11-09: past ~30 turns near moves alone reach 360 - kept well under it). The levels mode tells Muse the progress toward the need by the progress levels (below: a share of the need); amount levels (one ejaculation's) are empty: not sent. difficulty: points added at the start - candidate_over on the combos, plays_step on the plays - the coefficient 1 + per_point x points (at least min); a run's score = its total x the coefficient; a title for a run's score. Provisional values: replace freely (a new version).
